prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single, objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case and what you need (trial experience, high-value settlement history, handling of catastrophic injuries, etc.). I can help you find a great lawyer, but first here’s how to choose one and next steps.

What to look for
- Substantial car-accident experience (not just general practice).  
- Trial experience and a history of large verdicts/settlements if your case may be contested.  
- Board certification in Personal Injury Trial Law (if available) or other recognized credentials.  
- Good client reviews and peer ratings (Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo).  
- Resources to handle litigation (investigators, medical consultants, expert witnesses).  
- Clear contingency-fee agreement (typical TD/PI contingency 33%–40% depending on when case resolves) and transparent fee/expense policies.  
- Good communication and a clear point of contact (you want your calls/emails returned).

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases? How many similar cases have you taken to trial?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day — you or an associate?  
- What fee percentage do you charge? Who pays costs if we lose?  
- What is my case likely worth and what is the strategy?  
- Can you provide references or recent case results?

Where to find and check lawyers
- Texas State Bar lawyer search and disciplinary records.  
- Super Lawyers and Martindale‑Hubbell peer-review ratings.  
- Local Houston bar association referrals.  
- Online reviews (Google, Avvo) — read several, not just one.  
- Ask friends/family or doctors for referrals.

Important practical items
- Texas statute of limitations for most car-accident personal injury claims: 2 years from the date of the crash (act quickly).  
- Gather: police report, photos, videos, contact/insurance info, medical records and bills, pay stubs (lost wages), witness info.

Red flags
- Promises of a specific dollar amount up front.  
- Reluctance to put fee agreement in writing.  
- No office staff or unclear point of contact.  
- High-pressure sales tactics.

If you want, I can:
- Look up well-rated Houston personal injury attorneys and give you a short vetted list (tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether your case involves catastrophic injury, a commercial vehicle, uninsured/underinsured motorist, or other special issues).  
- Draft a list of specific questions tailored to your case for consultations.

Which would you like me to do?
